report.executive_summary: All four packages qualify independently: quality indices 87–98 clear the floor of 80 and defect counts 0–4 sit under the ceiling of 5, so reject_all stays idle. On the shared acceptance basis the energy minimum is unique — P3 at 10 Wh, ahead of P2 (22), P1 (28) and P4 (49) — so the candidate-ID tie-break is idle and the policy pick is P3. Analyst A's prose matches the trusted table on every value checked this round, a clean audit after round 2's errors; one residual item, exact bar proportionality in A's chart, is flagged as an open spot-check rather than a found defect.
report.figure_caption: Verified energy per acceptance batch, bars to scale (P3 10, P2 22, P1 28, P4 49 Wh) with successive gaps 12/6/21 Wh, beside the four-step verification workflow ending at policy pick P3.

recommendation.rationale: P3 is the unique lowest-energy qualifier at 10 Wh on the shared acceptance basis — 12 Wh ahead of P2 and 39 Wh ahead of P4 — and passes both thresholds (quality 97, defects 4). A's prose audit is clean this round; only chart proportionality remains open and does not change the pick.

sections.body: Recomputing from the trusted table: quality reads 87 (P1), 95 (P2), 97 (P3), 98 (P4) — all above 80. Defects read 0, 0, 4, 2 — all under 5. Spare defect margins are five slots for P1 and P2, three for P4 and one for P3; P3's margin is thinnest but its measured count of 4 satisfies the ceiling outright. No candidate fails either axis, so all four enter the energy ranking and reject_all remains idle.
sections.heading: Recomputed eligibility screen

sections.body: On the single shared basis — identical workload, output and test conditions — energy is the only minimized variable. Ascending: P3 10 Wh, P2 22, P1 28, P4 49. Successive gaps recompute as 12 Wh (P3 to P2), 6 Wh (P2 to P1) and 21 Wh (P1 to P4); the winner-to-last spread is 39 Wh. The minimum is unique, so the candidate-ID tie-break stays idle. Sensitivity: P3 needs a re-measurement above 22 Wh to lose the lead to P2; P4 would need to shed 39 Wh. These gaps are arithmetic consequences of the table, not new measurements.
sections.heading: Energy ranking and gap arithmetic

sections.body: A's prose is checked against the sources. The four table values, both thresholds, defect margins and energy gaps are stated correctly, and the energy-per-quality ratios (0.10, 0.23, 0.32, 0.50) recompute exactly. A correctly names the one policy route to a different pick — quality-first weighting would favor P4 at 98 — without asserting it as the client rule. This is a clean audit after round 2's false zero-defect claim and off-scale bars. Residual: A's chart caption states true values, but I could not confirm exact bar proportionality from delivered pixels; flagged as an open spot-check for handover, not a found defect.
sections.heading: Audit of analyst A's round-3 brief

sections.body: Established facts: the trusted table values, the all-qualify screen, the unique P3 10 Wh minimum, the 12/6/21 Wh gaps and the 39 Wh spread. Open questions: exact bar proportionality in A's chart (flagged for C's spot-check); batch-to-batch variance, since all values come from one acceptance batch; P3's one-slot defect margin under any re-measurement; and the unverified cost, delivery, maintenance and field-reliability factors, which cannot move the energy-first ranking. The handover to C carries the verified ranking, the clean A-prose audit and this flagged chart check.
